plan: This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so there's no incentive to shade my bid down or up. Bidding exactly my value of $39 maximizes my expected profit: I win whenever my value exceeds the others' bids, and I pay less than my value, ensuring non-negative profit whenever I win.

This is a second-price (Vickrey-style) auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid, not their own bid. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding higher than my value risks paying more than the item is worth to me; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $34, I will bid exactly $34.

This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction where I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid. The dominant strategy in this format is to bid exactly my true value, since my bid only determines whether I win, not what I pay. Bidding higher than my value risks winning at a price above my value (negative profit). Bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I should bid exactly $45, my true value, to maximize expected profit.
